title: Nitanshi Goel Closes Suneet Varma's Kashi Show at Lakme Fashion Week
excerpt: The Laapataa Ladies actor walked as showstopper in a wine-coloured fishtail lehenga as Varma revived a Varanasi-inspired collection built on a 32-year-old sourcing trip.
body:
• Laapataa Ladies actor Nitanshi Goel walked as showstopper for designer Suneet Varma's 'Kashi' collection at Lakme Fashion Week in New Delhi on Thursday.
  • She wore a wine-coloured, embellished fishtail lehenga with a draped top and plum and silver paillettes.
  • Varma built the collection on a textile-sourcing trip to Varanasi 32 years ago, reviving a tree-of-life cape motif from his own archive.
  • Lakme Fashion Week, held with FDCI, concludes Sunday with a finale by Amit Aggarwal.

Actor Nitanshi Goel, who broke through in the film Laapataa Ladies, closed designer Suneet Varma's show at Lakme Fashion Week in New Delhi on Thursday, walking as showstopper for his new collection, 'Kashi'. The showcase was held at the Taj Palace Hotel on the second day of the event, according to ANI's report from the show.

Goel wore a wine-coloured fishtail lehenga with heavy embellishment, finished with plum and silver paillettes. Reports differ slightly on the top — ANI described a strapless top with an attached drape, while the PTI report carried by Andhra Vilas described an off-shoulder draped top over a mermaid-tail skirt with sequin work throughout. Both accounts agree on the colour, the silhouette and the showstopper billing.

A collection built on a 32-year-old trip

Varma, a fixture of Indian fashion for more than three decades, took the collection's name and palette from Kashi — Varanasi — and from a sourcing trip he made there 32 years ago. He told reporters after the show that one of the final looks, a cape carrying a tree-of-life motif, revived artwork he had first used on a similar cape from that period, rebuilt this time against a Kashi landscape.

"For me, it is very nostalgic and beautiful."

— Suneet Varma, designer, speaking after the show

The wider collection worked in reds, purples, maroons and blacks, which ANI linked to the changing light over the Ganges. The line itself was ready-to-wear: draped saris, dhoti skirts, jackets, corset tops, tunics and trousers, detailed with embroidery, handwork and tassels. Femina's roundup of the week placed the show within a broader craft-led programme, noting Varma's effort to build a ready-to-wear vocabulary rooted in Indian aesthetics for a modern buyer.

Goel's turn in the spotlight

For Goel, the booking continues a rapid rise from film to fashion-week fixture. A Filmfare awardee for Laapataa Ladies, she was quoted in the PTI report saying she knew from Varma's vision that she would feel pretty in the look, adding that she was grateful and loved the collection. The choice of a young film actor rather than an established supermodel to close the show reflects how Lakme Fashion Week now uses cinema faces to carry designer stories to a wider audience.

Why this lands with diaspora readers

Heritage-led collections like Kashi are the segment of Indian fashion most visible abroad, where Banarasi textiles and temple-city references translate readily into occasion wear for weddings and festivals in the diaspora. Varma's stated aim — contemporary outfits that can be worn globally — is aimed squarely at that market: Indian construction and handwork, cut into silhouettes that work outside India as well as in it.

What comes next in the week

Lakme Fashion Week, run in partnership with the Fashion Design Council of India (FDCI), concludes on Sunday. The finale is by Amit Aggarwal, presenting the latest collection from his pret label AM.IT. Goel's showstopper turn gives the Varma show its headline moment, but the commercial test of Kashi will be how much of the ready-to-wear line reaches stores for the wedding and festive season ahead.
